source.title_on_document: Generative AI–Assisted Workflows in Architectural Conceptual Design: Performance, Creative Self-Efficacy, and Cognitive Load

supplement.where: The text cites an Appendix with Tables S1-S3 and Fig. S1; no URL is given for it. Data are on OSF (osf.io/b73jp).
supplement.holds: Table S1 (participant majors), Table S2 (NASA-TLX items), Table S3 (two-way ANOVA for the remaining outcomes), Fig. S1 (item-level NASA-TLX DiD).

paper_design_summary: Thirty-six students at Worcester Polytechnic Institute drew an initial architectural concept design for a research laboratory building without AI or precedent-search assistance, using wood blocks and a drawing tablet, then revised it for 30 minutes with a randomly assigned workflow: DALL-E 3 image generation inside ChatGPT-4 (GenAI, n = 18) or precedent search on ArchDaily (Control, n = 18). Eight judges rated all 72 drawings on a 1-5 rubric (clarity and legibility, complexity and detail, overall visual communication), averaged into a design-performance score; participants also reported creative self-efficacy and NASA-TLX workload after each phase. The analysis compares arms in each phase and uses a difference-in-differences across phases.

studies.label: Two-phase architectural conceptual design experiment (DALL-E 3 vs ArchDaily revision)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Revision-phase workflow: DALL-E 3 within ChatGPT-4 (GenAI group) versus precedent search on ArchDaily.com (Control group). Both arms did the initial design phase without AI or precedent-search assistance, using wood blocks and a drawing tablet.
assignment.quote: We first recruited 41 participants through flyers and snowball sampling. We then randomly assigned them to the Control group and GenAI group. However, 5 participants did not complete the study.
assignment.locator: p. 6 [printed 4], Section 3.1 Participants; also p. 10 [printed 8], Section 3.4.2 ('randomly assigned to either the control group or the treatment group')
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 14 [printed 12], Section 3.8: 'The study was not formally pre-registered.'

arms.name: GenAI
arms.description: Revised the initial design using DALL-E 3 within ChatGPT-4 to generate images by prompting; asked to consult at least five concepts.

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Revised the initial design using precedent search on ArchDaily.com; asked to consult at least five concepts.

participants.exclusions: 41 recruited and randomly assigned; 5 did not complete the study, leaving 36 (18 per arm). The paper also says the 36 'were formally considered and randomly assigned', so the count at assignment is stated ambiguously (41 or 36). Per-arm counts at assignment are not given. Screen recordings were missing for 2 GenAI and 1 Control participant; this affects only the interaction analyses (Sections 4.4-4.5), not the design-performance ratings.
participants.who: Students at Worcester Polytechnic Institute from a range of academic disciplines and years of study (not only architecture); Control 18 (8 female), GenAI 18 (9 female).
participants.quote: Thirty-six students were formally considered and randomly assigned to either the Control group or the GenAI group. The Control group consisted of 18 participants (8 females), while the GenAI group had 18 participants (9 females).

ai_tool.how_used: During the 30-minute revision phase, participants wrote their own prompts (none prescribed) to generate design images, and sketched their revised design on a drawing tablet; 3 to 26 prompts per participant.

task.description: Architectural concept design (building massing and geometry) for a research laboratory building at Gateway Park, WPI, sketched on a 15.6-inch digital drawing tablet; initial design without AI or precedent-search assistance, using wood blocks, then a revision with the assigned workflow.
task.duration: 30 min initial design phase plus 30 min revision phase in a roughly 1.5-hour individual session, after a one-hour group tutorial visit

outcomes.name: Design performance (revision-phase drawing; DiD across phases)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Eight judges (four design-studio professors, four senior architectural engineering students) each rated all 72 drawings (36 participants x 2 phases) in randomized order on a 1-5 scale for clarity and legibility, complexity and detail, and overall visual communication; the score is the mean of the three. The rubric rates visual-communication quality, not creativity or novelty. Average-measure ICC 0.157 (Phase 1) and 0.208 (Phase 2). DiD regression on participant-phase scores with SEs clustered by participant, standardized by the pooled SD of initial-phase scores. An exploratory two-way ANOVA (tool x median-split initial competency) is also reported.

contrasts.reported: Revision phase: Control 2.785 ± 0.361 vs GenAI 2.903 ± 0.433, p = 0.381, Cohen's d = 0.296 (n = 18 per arm). Initial phase: Control 2.921 ± 0.369 vs GenAI 2.819 ± 0.388, p = 0.426, d = -0.269. DiD = 0.583 SDs, 95% CI [-0.476, 1.643].
contrasts.locator: p. 15 [printed 13], Table 3; p. 16 [printed 14], Table 4 and Section 4.2

outcomes.name: General creative self-efficacy (self-report)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean of three 5-point items (Q3-Q5, adapted from Pretz and McCollum 2014) answered after each phase. Self-report, so it does not satisfy criterion 3; listed because it is the paper's headline significant result.

contrasts.locator: p. 15 [printed 13], Table 3; p. 16 [printed 14], Table 4 and Section 4.2

eligibility.reason: Randomized lab experiment (DALL-E 3 vs ArchDaily precedent search, individual assignment) with 36 people analyzed (18 per arm) out of 41 recruited and randomized (PDF pp. 6-7 [printed 4-5], Section 3.1; assignment also described on PDF p. 10 [printed 8], Section 3.4.2). Criterion 1 is met. Criterion 3 is met because judges scored the quality of participant-produced architectural designs using clarity and legibility, complexity and detail, and overall visual communication (PDF p. 11 [printed 9], Section 3.5 and Table 1). Under creativity-codebook.md, Sections 1, 3, and 6, quality of a single output qualifies as usefulness; a separate novelty or overall-creativity dimension is not required. Criterion 2 fails because 36 analyzed people is below 50, so core=no and context_class=none; the study belongs in the screening report as a small randomized experiment (codebook Section 3; form-spec.md, eligibility.core).

one_line_finding: With 18 students per arm, revising an architectural concept with DALL-E 3 instead of ArchDaily search did not significantly change judge-rated design performance (revision phase 2.903 vs 2.785, p = 0.381; DiD = 0.583 SDs, 95% CI [-0.476, 1.643]; PDF pp. 15-16, Tables 3-4), while general creative self-efficacy fell relative to control (DiD = -0.54 SDs, 95% CI [-1.068, -0.017]).
